karaṇḍaka.p: [Karaṇḍa+ka] (pu) CL=7 (1) A casket (or) a small bowl with a stand (painted with lacquer) (or) a wicker basket to put food (alms), etc., (2) King Karaṇḍaka.
pn: Karaṇḍaka 01. A hermitage (assamapada) near the Himālaya. The Bodhisatta, when born as an elephant as related in the Mātiposakajātaka (q.v.), returned to Karaṇḍaka after the death of his mother. The hermitage was the residence of five hundred ascetics, and the king, out of regard for the Bodhisatta, looked after them. Ja.iv.95.

Karandaka：1．Karandaka．-A hermitage （assamapada） near the Himalaya．The Bodhisatta，when born as an elephant as related in the Mātiposaka Jātaka （q．v．），returned to Karandaka after the death of his mother．The hermitage was the residence of five hundred ascetics，and the king，out of regard for the Bodhisatta，looked after them．J．iv．95．

karaṇḍa.p: [Kara+aṇḍa] (thī,pu) CL=7 [Moga, 7. 57. Karaḍi+ka. Kaccaññaḥ. 663.] (1) A casket (or) a large bowl with a stand and cover (usually of lacquer) for offering foods (alms) to monks. In Dhānasya, it is a small circular tray with a stem. (2) Cast off the skin (or) slough off the skin of a snake. (Ti) (3) Disgusted. See - Kāraṇḍava.
